notes:
Context: Saltire is a Europe-headquartered legal tech platform (case-law, contracts, internal memos). They need a RAG search layer that supports 9 languages with per-language precision tuning.

- Primary ask: embeddings + reranking stack that gives strong per-language recall/precision; measurable evals.
- Corpus: ~5M documents (mixed PDFs, OCRed images, contracts), steady ingest ~200k docs/day.
- Languages: en, fr, de, es, pt-BR, nl, it, zh-CN, ja. Will add sk/ru later.
- Index scale: starting POC ~50M embedding vectors after chunking; eventual goal 250M+ vectors.
- Latency targets: retrieval p99 <60ms (regional), reranker end-to-end p90 <200-250ms for en/fr/de; allow 300-350ms for CJK during evaluation.
- Throughput: peak 600-800 qps across EU; sustained 200 qps.
- Cost target: <$0.015 per query (emb+rerank) at scale; willing to trade for better recall on legal queries.
- Embedding model preferences: evaluating multilingual models (m-embed-xl, sentence-multilingual variants). Need advice on mixed-language cross-encoder reranker vs language-specific rerankers.
- Routing/fallback: prefer regional EU routing; fallback to smaller quantized models if Dedicated saturates. Important to keep consistent semantics across languages.
- Quality metrics: want per-language recall@10, precision@5, and question-type breakdown (statutory vs case law).
- Security/compliance: EU data residency required, SOC2 + ISO27001 mandatory, KMS for key management, SSO (SAML) integrated with Okta. Audit logs retention 2 years.
- POC scope: 2-week trial on Dedicated in eu-west with sample index (1M docs), per-language eval sets (50 queries/lang), run A/B: cross-encoder global vs language-specific cross-encoders. Deliverables: perf+cost matrix, precision/recall by language, recommended quantization & batching knobs.
- Quote from CTO: "we need parity in recall between EN and FR/DE; unacceptable to have Chinese precision degrade more than -10%".
- Sales notes: heavy procurement cycle; legal review flagged BYOD/external sharing clauses; procurement expects 60-day SLA negotiation.
- Technical open items: how Redwood Optimize recommends batching/cache config for mixed-language bursts; kernel/quantization guidance for zh/ja tokenization.
